name: Lumora Beauty

big_idea.title: The hour of light
big_idea.summary: Everyone looks their best in golden hour. Lumora, from lumen (light) and ora (hour), turns that light into a daily ritual: skincare that leaves every skin tone looking warm-lit and soft-focus, and a slow, warm hour you get back. Six products form one shelf that sets like the sun, from late light to dusk.
big_idea.the_look: Skin that looks warm-lit, even and soft-focus. The glow comes from skincare (vitamin C, carotenoid-rich oils, barrier care, light-diffusing textures), never from mica, glitter or self-tan. The glow formulas carry no tint; Apricity's sheer color comes from iron oxides.
big_idea.the_feeling: Ten slow minutes. Golden hour comes twice a day (after sunrise and before sunset), so the ritual does too. The evening half carries on beyond the face into the body (Gloaming oil) and a warm cup (Slow Hour golden milk). That is the Health in Health & Beauty, with no health claims attached.
ownable_devices: The logo: the 'o' in the wordmark is a sun touching the horizon.
The shelf: the six products step through a sunset, from sand to dusk, and each label's sun mark sinks one notch.
The homepage: color schemes warm as you scroll and reach dusk at the footer.

tagline_alternates.text: Every skin tone, in its best light.
tagline_alternates.use: Inclusivity messaging and casting brief (as a line, not as an H2)

positioning.audience: People aged 25 to 45, US-first, of every skin tone and gender, who want visible glow without glitter, tint or a ten-step routine. They are tired of clinical, white-lab aesthetics and of glow products that turn ashy on deep skin or orange on fair skin. They treat skincare as a small daily act of wellbeing and buy from premium DTC brands and specialty beauty retail.
positioning.promise: Skin that looks lit by late sun: warm, even and soft-focus, on every skin tone. Warm, never orange. Lit, never glittery.
positioning.price_tier: Premium, not luxury: $24 to $54. The hero serum is $54 for 30 ml. Free US shipping over $65 (20% above the hero), so any second product clears it.
why_different: A line organized by light: six numbered steps, late light to dusk, so the range explains itself.
Glow from skincare, not coatings: no mica, glitter or DHA anywhere in the line, and no tint in the glow formulas. Amber glass protects the light-sensitive vitamin C.
Inclusive by design: finishes tested on Fitzpatrick I to VI¹, the lip and cheek balm comes in three shades, and photography is cast across tones.
Beauty that bridges into wellbeing: a body ritual and an evening cup, without supplement claims.

voice.summary: Warm, unhurried, exact. Lumora sounds like a friend who notices the light: calm, sensory and precise. It does not hype.
principles: Second person for the reader, 'we' for the brand. Name the ingredient, the percentage and the hour.
Light and time are the shared vocabulary: late light, low sun, the last hour, twice a day, by week four. Use one light word per section at most.
Contrast pairs carry the promise: 'Warm, never orange.' 'Lit, never glittery.' Use one device per block.
Numbers beat adjectives, and every statistic carries its footnote in the same viewport.
A lexicon, used lightly. Product names are words for light, and each PDP opens with a one-line definition.
Headlines of six words or fewer, with one italic accent word that is always the last word. Eyebrows of two to four words.
No exclamation marks and no emoji. Sentence case, the Oxford comma and US spelling.
Claims are about appearance and feel only: looks, feels, helps, the look of. The brand never implies sun protection, tanning or after-sun care.
do: Use: warm, lit, soft-focus, satin, plush, slow, late light, twice a day, looks, feels, helps.
Use cosmetic wording: brightens the look of dull skin, evens the look of tone, helps replenish the moisture barrier, comforts dry-feeling skin, absorbs in seconds.
Put a superscript marker next to every statistic, with the method directly beneath the module, labeled illustrative placeholder data.
Show 'your daily SPF' as an unbranded morning step in ritual graphics.
Write 'formulated without X' and give the reason. List and explain every ingredient on its PDP.
Use specific verb CTAs that vary by job, with risk reversal next to the main CTA.
Keep Slow Hour sensory and sold as a food: ingredients, allergens and best-before, never benefits.
dont: Never say: sun-kissed, bronzed, tan, after-sun, flawless, miracle, treats, repairs, heals, anti-aging, detox, clean, chemical-free.
No SPF, UV, sun-protection or tanning implications, and no beaches, swimwear or bronzed skin.
No drug or structure/function claims (treat, cure, heal, collagen, anti-inflammatory, lightening or whitening).
No health, 'beauty from within', supplement or structure/function claims for Slow Hour.
No certification marks, press logos, 'clinically proven' or unsupported 'best'.
No 'up to' figures presented as typical. Report the exact figure or round down.
No fake urgency, countdowns or invented scarcity.
No hype words: elevate, unlock, indulge, luxurious, game-changer, holy grail.

sample_lines.line: Golden hour happens twice a day. So does the ritual.
The color is the ingredient: sea buckthorn's own carotenoids. No dyes.
gloaming (n.) the soft light after sunset. Also: your shoulders, after this oil.
We leave out mica and glitter. The glow should be your skin's, not a coating.
Scattered, skin looks flat. Returned, it looks lit.
You're $11 from free shipping. An Apricity would do it.
The Low Sun Letter. One note a fortnight, sent at your golden hour.
You've wandered past sunset. Back to the light.

display.why: Fraunces's SOFT axis at 100 rounds every serif and terminal: a warm, characterful serif that isn't another Didone.
display.source: OFL. Custom upload in Minimog: put the WOFF2 static instances in Content > Files, then Typography > Heading font > custom, one URL per weight (url@300, url@400); they render as M-Heading-Font. Declare the italic in Custom Liquid: @font-face{font-family:M-Heading-Font;font-style:italic;font-weight:300;src:url(...) format("woff2")}. Preload the Light WOFF2.
display.alternate_h1: Optional: instance the variable font with fonttools at opsz 96, SOFT 100, WONK 0 for a crisper H1.

typography.case_rules: Sentence case for headings, buttons, navigation and body copy; never all-caps headlines. Uppercase only for eyebrows (Figtree 600, +20%), the BEAUTY descriptor (+28%) and the format line on packs (+25%). Product names in title case, set in Fraunces Light Italic on labels and in running copy where specified. Ingredient names in lowercase in running copy (vitamin C keeps its capital). The wordmark is always lowercase and is never typed as live text.
typography.heading_accent: One italic word per heading, always the last word, in the scheme's accent color: Terracotta on Travertine and Linen; Clay on Sand and the Honey and Apricot washes; Dusk italic on Rose wash; Honey on Terracotta, Clay and Dusk (24 px and up only).

radius.rule: One radius token: 14 px for cards, tiles, images and drawers; 999 px for buttons, inputs and chips. Nothing else.
radius.minimog: --blocks-radius, --medium-blocks-radius and --pcard-radius set to 14 px; buttons and inputs at 999 px

container.minimog: container-fluid on every section, including the header, footer and PDP, so there is one left edge
container.note: 60 px gutters at 1440 and Minimog's native 15 px at 390, so stock and custom sections share one left edge

spacing.minimog_note: Global section spacing 0; each section owns its padding. Minimog scales section padding to min(value, 40px) on mobile.

construction.setting_sun_o: The 'o' is cut by a horizontal gap (the horizon) at 66.5 to 71% of the glyph box, about one third up its height. The sliver below the horizon turns Terracotta on light grounds and Honey on Dusk, like a sun touching the horizon.
construction.gap: 4.5% of the cap height, so it survives at 24 px wide. Below 80 px wide, use the one-color version with the gap widened to 7%.
construction.one_color: In one-color use (labels, foil, embossing) the cut stays and the color doesn't change.
construction.descriptor_lockup: Wordmark, a hairline, then BEAUTY in Figtree 600 at +28% tracking, with the optional line 'The hour of light' in Fraunces italic.

subjects: Skin in late sun at close and medium crops: cheekbones, jawlines, collarbones, shoulders, backs of necks, hands and wrists

photography.light: Low sun (side or back light), warm (about 3,000 to 3,800 K), with hard-edged leaf shadows. Some flare is fine. Indoor window light at golden hour as often as outdoor light.
photography.casting: Fitzpatrick I to VI in every set of four, ages 25 to 60, all genders. Real texture is kept: pores, fine hairs, freckles, stretch marks and hyperpigmentation. Minimal makeup, eyes closed or in profile, candid rather than posed.

Visible brands, logos or tattoos with text
Any image that could pass as a customer before-and-after

diagram.name: Scattered and returned
diagram.origin: Grafted from the Halo concept's 'radiance is optics' diagram, rewritten for Golden Hour. Educational only.
diagram.lead: Skin looks lit when light leaves it evenly. A dry, uneven surface scatters it. A smooth, hydrated, even surface sends it back together.

panels.label: Scattered
panels.caption: Dry, uneven surface
panels.drawing: Five parallel rays arrive from the left at 12° and leave in mixed directions as short broken strokes in Dusk 72%, off a fine irregular surface line

panels.label: Returned
panels.caption: Smooth, hydrated, even surface
panels.drawing: The same five rays leave together at the mirror angle as solid Terracotta strokes, off a level surface line

diagram.contrast_pair: Scattered, skin looks flat. Returned, it looks lit.
diagram.links_to_cards: Three of the four ingredient cards carry a small tag for the quality they help: Even (vitamin C), Smooth (apricot kernel oil) and Hydrated (ceramides + squalane). Each tag links to the matching PDP.
diagram.guardrail_line: This shows how skin looks in light, not sun protection. Your daily SPF still goes on every morning.

visual.format: Inline SVG in Custom Liquid. Two panels side by side on desktop (about 300 px tall in the 1320 px container); stacked on mobile.
visual.light_source: A Honey sun dot (the monogram disc) at the top left of each panel
visual.rays: 1.4 px strokes with round caps, the icon line weight. Terracotta #A8473B (5.4:1 on Linen) for incoming and returned rays; Dusk 72% #6E554C for scattered fragments.
visual.surface: A 1.4 px Dusk line. It is never the horizon arc, which is reserved for the two transitions.
visual.labels: Eyebrow style (Figtree 600, 12 px, +20%, uppercase) in Terracotta; captions in Figtree 13/20, Dusk 72%
visual.restraint: No gradient and no glow bloom (both are reserved). The section's one light word is 'glow', so the diagram adds no light metaphors.
visual.motion: On entering the viewport the returned rays draw in with stroke-dashoffset over 600 ms on the slow-sunset curve, with an 80 ms stagger. Fully drawn and static under prefers-reduced-motion.
visual.accessibility: role='img' with a title and description. Alt: 'Diagram: on a dry, uneven surface, light scatters in many directions; on a smooth, hydrated surface, it comes back together.'

diagram.compliance: Appearance and feel only: looks, feels, helps, the look of. No SPF, UV, reflect-the-sun or protection language, and no claims about the skin's structure.

signature_details: The sunset scroll: fourteen sections, one Minimog color scheme each, warming from Travertine through the Honey and Apricot washes to Terracotta, Clay and Dusk.
Setting-sun wordmark: a giant gradient lumora in the footer, clipped by a Honey horizon line, sinks 8% as the page ends.

The golden-hour clock: a Custom Liquid snippet prints today's golden hour for the visitor's time zone under the hero CTAs (NOAA solar formula, no location prompt). The same logic times the newsletter send.
The light changes: Minimog's second image on hover shows the same pack and crop in low sun, crossfading over 600 ms with a soft Honey under-glow.
Sun marks as the step system, on labels, cards, the PDP eyebrow, the mega menu and the ritual timeline.
The horizon arc: used exactly twice, under the hero and into the footer.
Leaf light from the rig: the gobo that shades the renders lies over two web sections at 6% multiply.
True italics: Fraunces SuperSoft Light Italic with WONK forms, so each heading's single accent word is a real italic.
Glowing buttons: the primary pill gains a 7 px Honey halo on hover; focus rings use the same halo with a contrast ring.
A lexicon on every PDP: a metafield-driven line under the title gives the name's definition in Fraunces italic.
Sunrise shipping bar: the cart's free-shipping progress fills with the golden-hour gradient.
Sun-dot footnotes: superscript markers sit in small Honey discs and link to the footnotes under each module.
Scattered and returned: a small diagram in the ingredients section shows why smooth, hydrated, even skin looks lit.
